problems.title: Test evenness directly
problems.question: Which of f=x³+x²,g=x³,h=x² are even?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: A function is even when $F(-x)=F(x)$ for every input.
steps: h(−x)=x²=h(x). g changes sign, while f(−x)=−x³+x² generally differs from f(x). Only h is even.

problems.title: Integer part of a fourth root
problems.question: Find floor(fourth-root(19)).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
steps: The root lies strictly between 2 and 3, so its integer part is 2.

problems.title: Rationalize a seventh root
problems.question: Which listed expression equals 1/seventh-root(8)?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
steps: The result is seventh-root(16)/2. Multiplying numerator and denominator by seventh-root(16) gives denominator seventh-root(128)=2.

problems.title: A trapezoid midline splits two areas
problems.question: Bases are 2,7. Find the ratio of the areas above and below the midline.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Midline length $m=(2+7)/2=4.5$; the two heights are h/2.
steps: The smaller-base part has area (2+4.5)h/4=13h/8. The larger-base part has area (4.5+7)h/4=23h/8. Their ratio is 13:23.

problems.title: A parallel line cuts off a parallelogram
problems.question: Trapezoid bases BC=2,AD=7. A line through C parallel to leg AB divides the area. Find the two-part ratio.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: The cut creates a parallelogram of base 2 and a triangle of base 7−2=5, sharing height h.
steps: The parallelogram area is 2h and triangle area 5h/2. Their ratio is 2:(5/2)=4:5.

problems.title: Combine evenness with periodicity
problems.question: f is even with period 6. If f(13)=19, find f(11).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.

problems.title: Distance between two graph intercepts
problems.question: Find the distance between axis intercepts of y=1−1/(x−1).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Find each intercept by setting the other coordinate to zero; use distance formula.
steps: At y=0, x=2. At x=0, y=2. The points are (2,0),(0,2), whose distance is √8=2√2.

problems.title: Real cube roots preserve the negative sign
problems.question: Simplify [cube-root(40)+cube-root(−5)]cube-root(2).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
steps: The bracket is cube-root(5). Multiplying by cube-root(2) gives cube-root(10).

problems.title: Three of four diagonal triangle areas
problems.question: The diagonals of a trapezoid make four triangles, three of whose areas are 1,3,9. Find total area.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: The two side-adjacent triangles have equal areas t; the base-adjacent areas u,v satisfy $uv=t^2$.
steps: The repeated area must be 3, since 1×9=3². Repeating 1 or 9 would contradict the product relation.
Thus the four areas are 1,3,3,9, totaling 16.

problems.title: An inscribed quadrilateral area by subtraction
problems.question: K∈AB,M∈BC,N∈AC; AK:KB=2:7,BM:MC=1:2,CN:NA=5:4. Find area(AKMN)/area(ABC).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: For a vertex triangle, the area ratio equals the product of its two side fractions.
steps: Remove triangle BKM, fraction (7/9)(1/3)=7/27, and triangle CMN, fraction (2/3)(5/9)=10/27.
The remaining quadrilateral fraction is 1−17/27=10/27.

problems.title: An absolute value folds a parabola upward
problems.question: f(x)=x². Find the range of y=|f(x−2)−3|.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: The function is $|(x-2)^2-3|$, always nonnegative.
steps: It reaches zero at x=2±√3 and grows without bound as |x| grows. By continuity it attains every value from zero upward.

problems.title: Symmetry around a shifted pole
problems.question: For f(x)=(x−20)^(−20), which listed equality holds?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: $f(x)=1/(x-20)^{20}$, defined for x≠20 and symmetric about x=20.
steps: 17 and 23 are equally distant from 20, so f(17)=f(23)=1/3²⁰. The other listed input pairs are not equally distant from 20.

problems.title: A point shared by odd powers only
problems.question: Which point belongs to y=xⁿ for every odd positive integer n but no even positive integer n?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: $(-1)^n=-1$ for odd n and +1 for even n.
steps: Thus (−1,−1) has exactly the required property.

problems.title: Trapezoid area from two diagonal projections
problems.question: A trapezoid has height 1 and diagonals √5,√10. Which listed area is possible?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Horizontal diagonal projections have magnitudes $\sqrt{5-1}=2$ and $\sqrt{10-1}=3$.
steps: If both diagonals point across the trapezoid in the usual opposite horizontal directions, the base sum is 2+3=5, giving area 5/2.
A strongly leaning trapezoid can instead have base sum |3−2|=1 and area 1/2. Only 5/2 appears among the choices.
problems.answer: 5/2 among the choices; possible areas are 1/2 and 5/2.

problems.title: Area from lengths along two altitudes
problems.question: In acute ABC, altitudes AM,CN meet at H. AH=HM=2,CH=4,HN=1. Find area.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Use coordinates along AM and Pythagoras, followed by collinearity of A,N,B.
steps: Set H=(0,0),A=(0,2),M=(0,−2). Since C lies on the horizontal side BC and CH=4, take C=(2√3,−2).
N lies beyond H on line CH, with HN=CH/4. Thus N=(−√3/2,1/2). Line AN meets y=−2 at B=(−4√3/3,−2).
BC=10√3/3 and altitude AM=4. Area=BC×4/2=20√3/3=20/√3.

problems.title: Range of a fractional-linear function
problems.question: Find the range of (3x+2)/(5x+4).
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Solve $y=(3x+2)/(5x+4)$ for x.
steps: (5y−3)x=2−4y. When y=3/5 this equation is impossible. Every other y gives x=(2−4y)/(5y−3), and this x cannot equal the excluded −4/5.
Hence precisely 3/5 is missing from the range.

problems.title: A nested root needs absolute values for negative inputs
problems.question: Simplify fifth-root[a·fourth-root(a·cube-root(a))] over its real domain.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Put $u=\sqrt[3]a$, so a=u³ and $\sqrt[4]{a\sqrt[3]a}=\sqrt[4]{u^4}=|u|$.
steps: The outer radicand is u³|u|, so the result is sign(u)|u|^(4/5)=sign(a)|a|^(4/15), with value zero at a=0.
For a≥0 this becomes fifteenth-root(a⁴), the listed intended answer. For a<0 the original is negative, whereas that listed expression is positive.
problems.note: No sign restriction on a is printed. The expression is real even for negative a, so the listed nonnegative-root simplification needs the extra condition a≥0.

problems.title: Integer and fractional parts constrain a product
problems.question: x=floor(x),y={y},x+3y=199. How many different values can xy take?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: x is an integer, and y={y} means $0\le y<1$.
steps: Thus 196<x≤199, giving x=197,198,199 with y=2/3,1/3,0 respectively.
Their products are 394/3,66,0, all distinct.

problems.title: An incircle fixes a right-trapezoid area
problems.question: An incircle centre is √6 from a right-angle vertex and 2√3 from an acute-angle vertex. Find trapezoid area.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: At vertex angle θ, centre distance $=r/\sin(\theta/2)$.
steps: At 90°, distance=r√2=√6, so r=√3 and height=2√3. At the acute vertex, distance=2√3=2r, giving its angle 60°.
The slanted leg is height/sin60°=4 and vertical leg 2√3. Tangentiality makes base sum equal leg sum=4+2√3.
Area=(base sum)height/2=(4+2√3)√3=4√3+6.

problems.title: A median in half of a parallelogram
problems.question: ABCD is a parallelogram, M is AD’s midpoint, CD=10,BD=24,BM=13. Find area.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: In triangle ABD, Apollonius gives $AD^2=2AB^2+2BD^2-4BM^2$.
steps: Triangle ABD has sides 10,24,26 and is right, with area 10×24/2=120. The parallelogram has twice that area, 240.

problems.title: An odd periodic extension
problems.question: An odd, period-4 function equals x²−2x on [0,2]. Find its full range.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
steps: Oddness supplies the opposite values [0,1] on [−2,0]. This interval of inputs covers a full period, and periodicity introduces no new output values.

problems.title: A line and its inverse share every intercept
problems.question: For every real b, y=kx+b and its inverse have the same y-axis intercept. Find k.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: An inverse requires k≠0 and is $y=(x-b)/k$, with intercept −b/k.
steps: Require b=−b/k for every b. Setting b=1 forces k=−1, and then the equality holds for all b.

problems.title: When input and output absolute values agree
problems.question: For quadratic f(x)=ax²+bx+c,a≠0, graphs |f(x)| and f(|x|) coincide. What must hold?
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: The right side is even, so $f(x)^2=f(-x)^2$ for all x.
steps: The difference of those squares factors as 4bx(ax²+c). Because a≠0, it vanishes identically only if b=0.
Then f is even, and the equality reduces to |f(x)|=f(x), requiring f≥0 everywhere. Thus a>0 and discriminant D≤0 (equivalently c≥0).

problems.title: Seven areas in a twice-as-wide trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid’s large base is twice its small base. Draw both diagonals and its midline, giving seven regions. Sorted by area, the middle region has area 60. Find the second-smallest.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: Normalize the bases to 1,2 and height h; area ratios do not change under this affine scaling.
steps: The diagonal intersection is h/3 below the small base. The midline is h/2 below it. Computing triangle and trapezoid areas gives: lower corner triangles h/8 each, lower central region 5h/8, top triangle h/6, tiny middle triangle h/24, and two upper side regions 5h/24 each.
In increasing order the areas are (h/24)×[1,3,3,4,5,5,15]. Thus the middle is 4 parts and the second is 3 parts.
The required area is 60×3/4=45.

problems.title: Maximum tangent of a diagonal angle
problems.question: A parallelogram has sides 1,3. Find the maximum tangent of the smaller angle between its diagonals.
problems.idea: Use the exact definition or theorem, checking domains, signs and possible geometric arrangements.
formulas: For diagonals p=u+v,q=u−v, $|p\cdot q|=8$ and $|p\times q|=2S$.
steps: tanθ=|p×q|/|p·q|=S/4. The parallelogram area S≤1×3=3, with equality when adjacent sides are perpendicular.
Therefore the maximum tangent is 3/4, attained by a 1-by-3 rectangle.
